note: Written through the gateway by GET /api/eval?task=dialogue; beats checked word for word.

lines.text: Morning, everyone. Can you hear me okay? I'm seeing the little bars move but I never trust them.
Yep, loud and clear here. Morning, Priya.
Morning. Hi, Marcus. Sorry, I'm still sorting out my headphones, give me one second.
No rush, we're waiting for a couple of people anyway.
Okay, there. Can you hear me now? It was on the laptop speakers before, so it probably sounded like I was in a tunnel.
A bit, yeah. You sound normal now.
Good. Mm, I hate that. You join a call and you're the one echoing at everybody.
Hi all. Sorry, can someone confirm I'm not on mute? My screen says I'm not, but it said that last time too.
We can hear you, Daniel.
Great. Morning. I had to switch rooms, so if my camera looks strange, that's why.
It looks fine. A bit dark, maybe. You're mostly a silhouette with a nice lamp behind you.
Ha, right. Let me turn the light around. Is that better?
Much better. Now I can see your face.
Is that a plant behind you? That's new.
It's not new, it's just that it was always out of frame. It's been there a while, it's suffering.
Well, it looks okay from here.
Somebody just joined by phone. I'm seeing a Call-in user 2 in the list. Is that one of ours?
Hello? Hi, yes, it's me, I'm on the phone only. I couldn't get the video link to open, sorry.
No problem at all, welcome. Can you hear all of us okay?
I can hear, but there's a bit of a crackle. It comes and goes.
We can hear you fine, just a little crackle on our side too. Should be okay.
Okay, good. I'll stay quiet unless I have something, I don't want to talk over anybody on this line.
That's fine. Just jump in if you need to. If we can't hear you properly, we'll tell you.
Okay, thanks.
Is anyone else's screen share stuck? Mine's showing the tab from the previous meeting.
Not sharing anything yet, so mine's fine. Maybe just stop sharing and start again?
Yeah, let me do that. Okay, it's gone. Nothing to share yet anyway, so never mind.
Quick one before we start. Did the weather mess up anyone's trip in this morning? Mine took forever.
Mm-hm, mine too. The rain was awful. I nearly turned back.
I worked from home, so I only heard about it. Sounds unpleasant.
I took the long way round and I'm still thawing out. Anyway, I think we're all here. Shall we start?
Go for it.
Agenda is the movers, the X-ray room, the licence, the building handover and the cutover weekend.
Sounds like a full list for the time we have.
It is, so let's keep each one moving. First, the movers. Marcus, where are we with the quote?
The movers quote came in at forty two thousand dollars, which is twelve thousand over what we budgeted for the move.
Sorry, say that again? Forty two, and twelve over?
Yeah. Forty two thousand is what they're asking. It's twelve thousand more than the move budget.
Right. So it's not a small miss. That's a good chunk.
That's a real problem, we can't absorb twelve thousand from contingency this early.
I know. I'm not happy about it either. I did read it twice to make sure I wasn't misreading a line.
Is it a single number, or did they break it down at all? I'm wondering where the twelve thousand is hiding.
They did break it down. That's the thing I wanted to say next.
They priced weekend overtime for the whole job. If we move the non-clinical rooms on a weekday it should drop.
Oh, so the overtime is the driver, not the amount of stuff they're carrying.
That's how I read it. They assumed everything goes over the weekend, so everything got the overtime rate.
Mm-hm. And the non-clinical rooms, that's the offices, storage, that sort of thing?
Yes, the rooms where nobody's seeing patients. Those don't need the weekend, in my view.
Makes sense. Although I'd want to know how much of the forty two thousand those rooms actually are. If it's a small slice, moving them on a weekday won't save much.
That's fair, and honestly I don't have that split yet. It's why I think we need them to price it again.
Do we know they'd even be willing to split it? Some movers just want one big job.
I don't know. I haven't asked yet. I only know what they put on the quote.
Okay, so that's an open question, whether they'll price it that way. But the logic holds up, weekend rate on everything is going to be more than a mix.
Sure. I'm not arguing with the logic. I just don't want us to count on a saving we haven't seen.
Agreed, and I'm not promising one. I said it should drop, not that it will.
Fine, that's all I wanted to hear.
Sorry, can I ask something? Is the forty two thousand the final price, or is it just the first quote?
It's the quote we have so far. Nothing is final. It's just the number they came back with.
Okay, understood. Thanks.
And twelve over budget, that's over the move budget only, right? Not over everything.
Right. The move budget. That's the figure I compared it with.
And I'll say it again, we don't want to dip into contingency for this. It's far too early in the project to be spending that.
No, I agree. If contingency goes now, then we've got nothing left for the surprises.
There are always surprises.
Always.
Okay. Marcus, please get a revised quote with the weekday split by Friday the fourth.
Got it. I'll ask them to show the weekday and weekend parts separately so we can see what we're looking at.
Good, that's what I'd want. Anything else on the movers before we go on?
Not from me.
No, I'm fine.
Okay. Next, the X-ray room. Siti?
The X-ray machine has to be moved and recalibrated by the vendor's own engineers, Radix Imaging.
So we can't have the movers touch it at all?
That's how I understand it. It's the vendor's engineers who do the move and the recalibration. It's not something the general movers would do.
Right, okay. I'll keep that in mind for the quote, then. Sorry, just thinking aloud.
So the X-ray isn't even in that forty two thousand?
I don't know what's in the movers quote, Daniel. That's more a question for Marcus.
I'd have to look at the line items again. I don't want to say yes or no off the top of my head.
Fair enough. Not trying to open a can of worms, I was just wondering.
Let's not go down that road right now. Siti, carry on.
Their engineers are booked out most of February, so there's a chance we don't get a slot before the cutover.
Booked out most of February. So it's not that they're fully booked, it's most of the month.
Yes, most of it. That's what they said. So there's a chance, it isn't certain, that we miss the cutover.
Mm. And how firm is that? Did they say that in writing, or was it a call?
It was a conversation. I wouldn't call it a firm no. It's more that the calendar looks tight for them.
Tight meaning they might still find a slot?
Might. That's why I said there's a chance. I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, or better.
Right. Sorry, I'm just trying to work out how worried to be.
I think somewhere in the middle. Concerned, not panicking.
If imaging isn't ready on day one we'd have to send patients to the old site, which defeats the purpose.
Yeah, that would be the worst version. You move everything and then people still have to go back to the old place for their scans.
Exactly. And it's confusing for patients too. They'd turn up at one place and get told to go to the other.
Mm-hm. That's not a great first impression for the new site.
No. And it's the point of the whole move, so I don't want us to treat it as a side issue.
Sorry, just to be sure I follow. The machine itself, it can't be used at all until their engineers have done it?
That's the way I understand it. They move it, they recalibrate it. Until then, we don't have imaging at the new place.
Okay. Thank you, that's clear.
Can I ask something a bit awkward? Is there any way around the vendor? Like, a different company doing the recalibration?
The way it was put to me, it's the vendor's own engineers. So I wouldn't count on anyone else.
Okay. That's what I thought, I just wanted to hear it said.
And I'm guessing it's no use asking them to squeeze us in?
I mean, we can ask. I think that's more or less what I'd like to do.
Go on, what's your plan?
I'll ask Radix to hold two provisional dates for us, and I'll come back next week.
Good. Thank you.
Provisional, so they're not committing, just holding them?
That's the idea. Holding, not confirmed. We'd see where we are after that.
Better than nothing. At least we'd have something on their calendar.
Right. It's one of those where I'd rather we asked early and were told no than found out late.
Agreed. That's my thinking too.
Okay. I'm fine with that. Moving on?
Yes. The licence transfer. Daniel, you spoke to the regulator?
Yes. The healthcare licence has to be transferred to the new address before we see any patient there.
So not a single patient at the new place until that's done.
That's how it was explained to me. Before any patient, so no gentle start with a few appointments.
Mm. That puts a lot on that one step.
It does. It's a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have.
Okay. And the timing on their side?
Our plan assumes the ministry processes the transfer within six weeks of us filing it.
Our plan assumes, so that's us assuming. Did they actually say six weeks?
I'd put it as what our plan assumes. I wouldn't claim it's a promise from them. That's the number we're working with.
Okay, that's what I wanted to be clear on. It's an assumption.
Right, and we don't know if it could be shorter or longer.
I can't say it either way. All I can tell you is what the plan uses.
Six weeks from when? Have we filed yet?
Not yet, we file once the floor plan is final, which should be next Monday.
So the six weeks hasn't started.
No, it hasn't started. The clock begins when we file.
And we file when the floor plan is final. So the floor plan is what everything hangs on.
Yes. It's linked, that's the order. Floor plan final, then we file, then the ministry's time starts.
And next Monday is for the floor plan being final, is that right? Not for the transfer to be done.
Right, next Monday is just the floor plan. That's when we file, not when we hear back.
Okay, I wanted to be sure I'd understood. It's easy to hear that and think it's sorted.
Yeah. It's the start, not the finish.
Sorry, one more from me. When you say the floor plan, is that the final layout of the new place?
Yes, the layout of the new site. We file once that's final.
Okay. Thanks, that helps.
Going back to the X-ray for a second, because it's the same pattern. We've got things waiting on other people's calendars.
True. Both the licence and the imaging depend on someone else's time, and we don't control either.
Mm-hm. Though at least the licence has a number attached, even if it's only our assumption.
Yes, that's fair. Imaging has a bit less to hold on to.
I'd still feel better if the regulator had said it themselves.
I hear you. It's what our plan assumes, and I'm not going to dress it up as more than that.
No, that's honest, and that's what I need from you. I'd rather we know exactly what is and isn't solid.
Understood.
Building handover from the landlord.
Right, yeah. I've been waiting to get to this one, because it's the one that everything else sits behind.
Go on then, where are we with it?
So, let me just find my notes. Sorry, one second. Okay.
Take your time. I'm still scrolling through the last page of the agenda anyway.
Same, I had the wrong tab open.
We can't start the fit-out of the treatment rooms until the landlord hands over level five, and they've said the fifteenth of January.
Mm-hm. So that's the date they've given us. Is that, like, a firm date, or is it more of a target?
That's the thing, they've said it, but I wouldn't call it firm. It's what they've said to us, that's all I can tell you.
Said how, though? On a call, or in an email?
Mostly on a call. I did get a short message afterwards but it didn't really repeat the date. That's what's bothering me a bit.
Right, okay. So it's a verbal thing at the moment.
More or less, yeah.
Sorry, this is the call-in user. Can everyone hear me okay? I think I got cut off a second ago.
We can hear you fine. Go ahead.
Thanks. I just wanted to check I've got it right. The treatment rooms can't be started until level five is handed over, is that right?
Yes, that's it. The fit-out of the treatment rooms waits for the handover of level five.
And the handover is the fifteenth of January. Okay. Sorry, the line's a bit crackly, I wanted to be sure I heard the date properly.
No, you heard it right. Fifteenth of January.
Great, thank you. I'll stay on mute.
No, that's fine, ask whenever. It's better to check than to guess.
Can I ask something? When you say we can't start, is that a hard stop, or is it more that we'd rather not?
It's a hard stop as far as I understand it. We don't have access to the level until they hand it over.
Okay, so no partial access, nothing like that.
Not that anyone's offered. I haven't asked about it, to be honest, and I'm not going to promise anything on that.
No, no, I'm not asking you to. I just wanted to be clear in my own head what we're dealing with.
It's a fair question though. If it's a hard stop then the date is the whole story.
Yeah. It is. That's why I keep going on about it.
You're not going on about it. It's the right thing to be going on about.
I guess what I'm wondering is, when they said the fifteenth, did they say it like they were sure?
They sounded sure. I mean, nobody said anything like maybe or hopefully. But I don't want to read too much into a tone of voice on a phone call.
Fair enough. I'd probably do the same, I'm just trying to picture how it went.
Was it the same person each time, that you've been speaking to?
It's been a couple of people, yeah. The one who gave me the date is the property manager, so that's the person I'd go back to.
Okay. Good. That makes sense.
So everything from the treatment rooms onwards hangs on that date.
Yeah, that's how I see it.
Everything onwards, meaning the rooms and whatever comes after them.
Right. I'm not trying to list it all out, I'm just saying that's the thing the rest is waiting on.
No, understood. I wasn't trying to add anything, I just wanted to say it back.
It's a bit uncomfortable, isn't it, that it's all sitting on one date that we only have by phone.
It is. I agree with that.
Which is probably the point of getting it written down.
Mm. Yeah.
Is there any downside to asking for it in writing? Like, would they take it badly?
I don't think so. It's a normal thing to ask. If anything it's more awkward for us not to ask.
Yeah, true. I just didn't know how the relationship was with them.
It's fine. It's been perfectly civil.
Civil, okay. That's a ringing endorsement.
Ha, no, it's fine, honestly. It's normal. They're a landlord.
Marcus, are you comfortable taking that one?
Yeah, I'll get the handover date in writing from their property manager.
Good. Thank you.
And once it's in writing, that's the date we all work to, I suppose.
Well, it's the date we've been given. If the writing says something different, I'll say so. But I'm expecting it to say the same thing.
Of course. We'll deal with that if it happens.
Fine by me.
Can I just say, from my side, that sounds sensible. It's good to have it on paper.
Thanks. I think we're all agreed on that. Anything else on the handover before I move on?
Not from me.
No, I'm good.
I'm done on that one.
Okay. Last one, the cutover weekend. We need to lock it.
Finally. I've been wanting this one nailed down for ages.
I know. I think we've gone round it a couple of times now.
We have. I think we left it open last time on purpose, to see what else came up.
Yeah, that's right. So let me just put the options back on the table so we're all looking at the same thing.
Sure. I'm happy to be walked through it again, I'd rather we all agree what the choices are.
We said either the thirteenth and fourteenth of February or the week after.
Right. So it's those two, and not any others.
Those two, that's what we said.
Just so I'm clear, the week after means the weekend after the thirteenth and fourteenth?
That's how I took it, yeah. The next weekend along.
That's how I understood it too.
Okay, good. I wanted to make sure I wasn't picturing something different.
Sorry to jump in again. So the choice is between two weekends, one in February and then the one straight after it?
Yes, exactly that. The thirteenth and fourteenth, or the one after.
Thanks. That's all I wanted to confirm.
Does anyone have a strong view on it? I don't think I do, personally.
I don't, either. I'd go with whichever one works for the people who are actually going to be there.
Daniel, you've got the best sense of the staffing side. What are you thinking?
Well, I was going to say, I did look at this, and the week after is the problem.
The week after clashes with the school holidays, half the nurses are on leave.
Oh. Half? That's a lot.
That's what I'm hearing. I'm not saying it's an exact number, but it's about half.
That's quite a clash, then.
Yeah. It's not that people couldn't be asked, it's just that you'd be asking a lot of them when they've planned to be away.
No, I get that. People book that kind of time off well ahead.
Right. And it's the nurses, so it's the people we most need on the day.
Mm-hm. That's a good point. I hadn't put that together with the dates.
Neither had I, to be fair. I was only thinking about it from the building side.
So the thirteenth and fourteenth looks better on that score.
It does for me. It doesn't clash with the holidays.
Does anyone see a reason to prefer the week after? I want to give it a fair go before we decide.
I can't think of one. I mean, you'd have a bit more time, I suppose, if it were later.
Is that worth a lot, though? If half the nurses are away.
No, probably not. I was only thinking aloud. It doesn't outweigh the leave.
And I'd not want to put the nurses in a spot where they're having to cancel their plans.
No, I agree. That's not a good way to start in a new place.
Can I just check one thing, going back to the first topic? The date we're working with for the building is the fifteenth of January.
Yes, that's the handover date they've given us.
And the cutover would be the thirteenth and fourteenth of February. I'm only asking because I want to be sure the order makes sense, handover first and then cutover.
Yeah, the handover comes first, obviously. It's the earlier date.
Right. And I suppose that's another reason to get the handover date in writing.
Yeah, that's the link. If the handover date moves, then we'd need to look at things again.
Okay. I wasn't trying to start a worry, I just wanted to say it out loud.
No, that's fine. It's good to say it out loud. And that's what the written date is for.
So we're going on the basis that the date holds.
On the basis of what they've told us, yes. And Marcus will confirm it.
Yep.
Sorry, one more from me. Is today the point where we pick the weekend, or are we just discussing it?
Today, that's the idea. We said we'd lock it, so I'd like to get to a decision before we finish.
Okay, that's clear. Thank you.
Right, so does anyone want to say anything more before Priya asks?
Nothing from me.
No. I've said my bit.
Okay then, decision: the cutover weekend is the thirteenth and fourteenth of February. Everyone okay?
Yes, agreed.
Agreed.
Yep, fine by me.
And from me, that's fine too.
Good. Thanks, everyone. That's the one I wanted to get done.
It's a relief, honestly. It felt like it was hanging around.
It did. It's nice to have it written down somewhere, even if it's only in the notes.
It will be in the notes, yes.
Can I just say it back so I've got it straight? Cutover is the thirteenth and fourteenth of February, and I'm chasing the written handover date.
Yes, that's it. That's the whole thing.
Sounds right to me.
Same.
Okay. I think that's us. Thanks for your time, everyone, and thanks to our call-in user for joining.
Thanks for having me. Bye, everyone.
Thanks, all. Speak soon.
Bye, take care.
Bye, all.
Bye, everyone.
